history.summary: Modern hilltop Shiva temple in Jatoli village, ~6-7 km from Solan on the Solan-Rajgarh road, founded by Swami Krishnananda Paramhans (arrived 1950; foundation laid 1973 or 1974; he died 1983). Built over ~39 years entirely on public donations, it is popularly claimed to be the tallest Shiva temple in Asia at ~111-122 ft (figures vary by source, verify). Architecture is South-Indian Dravidian style with three consecutive pyramids bearing Ganesha, Shesh Nag and a golden kalash/Trident. Name derives from Shiva's 'jata' (matted locks); legend says Shiva meditated here and a natural shivlinga manifested. Local lore claims the temple stones ring like a damru when tapped. The sanctum houses a rare crystal shivlinga; Swami Krishnananda's meditation cave survives in the complex.

name: Jatoli Shiv Temple
town_description: Jatoli is a small village on the Solan-Rajgarh road in Solan district, Himachal Pradesh, set amid forested hills about 6-7 km from Solan town. It is known almost entirely for the Jatoli Shiv Temple that towers over the hilltop. The area offers panoramic views of the surrounding valleys and is a popular day-trip stop from Solan.

travel.airport: Chandigarh International Airport, ~80 km (verify); Shimla airport (Jubbarhatti) ~57 km (verify)
travel.road: ~6-7 km from Solan on the Solan-Rajgarh road; stairs from the road lead up to the temple

visitor_information.best_time: Year-round; October to March for the clearest views
